name: IEC adder (Σ)
summary: IEC element marked Σ that adds binary words P and Q with carry-in CI and carry-out CO.
description: The adder qualifier is the capital sigma. Inputs are grouped into P and Q words with binary weights, plus a carry input CI; outputs give the sum with weights and a carry output CO. TI's overview lists Σ alongside P-Q for subtraction and CPG for look-ahead carry generation.

Adders on drawings usually belong to arithmetic sections of logic boards, counters with preset arithmetic, or illustrations of PLC arithmetic blocks. The carry chain between stages should be drawn so that the word length is obvious.
The symbol does not state whether the device uses ripple or look-ahead carry internally. Speed depends on that and on the word length.
readingNotes: Check carry-in and carry-out connections between stages.
Bit weights define the word order.
drawingChecklist: Label P, Q, CI and CO.
Show the carry chain for multi-device words.
distinction: A subtracter carries the P-Q qualifier instead; Σ marks an adder.
